extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, law students, and judges researching patent doctrines
extracted.subtask_description: An index-style excerpt from a patent law treatise listing doctrinal criteria and standards for patentability, ownership, defenses, remedies, procedure, and post-grant corrections (e.g., re-issue). Useful as a reference for evaluating patents, infringement, and related remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patented invention — nature determined by construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the invention claimed in the patent; its nature is determined by construction given to the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presumed to differ from all prior inventions; not to infringe prior patents; enjoyment by owner unrestricted by law except as its nature restricts; the patented invention is twofold (the invention and the monopoly). Property in the invention originates in the inventive act and is the right to practise the invention; property in the monopoly is created by the patent and is the right to prevent others from practising the invention. Transferability and limits (e.g., federal statutes) and remedies for injuries noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patented articles — stamping and effect of failure to stamp
rubrics_metrics.description: Issues concerning stamped patented articles and the effect of failing to stamp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a topic (cross-references) — guidance would include legal consequences for failure to mark/stamp patented articles (see stamping doctrine entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentees — who may be patentee and scope of rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Classes of patentees; who may be patentee and how title vests at grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be earliest conceiver if diligent in reduction; may be alien, infant, married woman; Patent Office employee may not be; legal title vests at grant; rights depend on legal construction of patent; patentee is chargeable with notice of what patent contains; bound by actual invention and by claims; may discard unclaimed matter; estopped to claim matter covered by prior patent; must amend faulty description/claim without unreasonable delay; presumptions about ownership until transfer proved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patented invention — reachability by local process and remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether patented invention can be reached by local process and availability of remedies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cannot be reached by local process; not liable to execution; not exempt from attachment by intrinsic nature; may be subject to creditors' claims only by assignment in equity; not subject to sale by probate or bankruptcy courts; not an asset of decedent's estate; injuries to patentees are remediable by law (see cross-references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pendency of former suit — pleading and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: How to plead pendency of a former suit and its effect in equity and law actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pendency may be pleaded (references). Suit in one district in equity no bar to another; at law no bar to suit in another; grounds for stay of decree in another; see cross-references to actions at law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pendente lite transfer — effect on suit and notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Effect of transfer pendente lite on suits and requirement of notifying defendant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfers pendente lite do not affect the suit; defendant to be notified; see related entries on assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perfect patent — meaning and definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition and meaning of a 'perfect patent'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perfect patent defined; contrasts with imperfect patents (see re-issue). See cross references for legal implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for patent — requisites
rubrics_metrics.description: Requisites for a petition (application) for patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a topic (see application requirements in cited sections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Piratical use — not public use defense
rubrics_metrics.description: Pirated/fraudulent use does not constitute public use for defense against patent validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Piratic or fraudulent uses are not public uses; see doctrine on public use and abandonment (citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plaintiffs in infringement actions — pleading, joinder, and proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules about plaintiffs suing for infringement in law and equity, joinder, parties, and required pleadings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In actions at law (citations) and in equity (citations); not presumed able to sell all defendant sold or make all profit defendant did; must sue in their own names; joinder of legal and equitable owners; nonjoinder/misjoinder consequences; may be enjoined from suing defendant's vendees pending suit; see cross-references to related doctrines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan or theory — not an invention
rubrics_metrics.description: A mere plan or theory of action or construction is not an invention; may be protected by copyright but not patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans/theories are not patentable; protection falls under copyright, not patent law; see citations discussing distinctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pleadings not evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Pleadings are not evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pleadings have no evidentiary weight (citation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Police power of the States — not curtailed by Patent Law
rubrics_metrics.description: State police power is not curtailed by patent law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent law does not limit States' police power (citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Possession of infringing device — evidentiary weight
rubrics_metrics.description: Possession of an allegedly infringing device may be evidence of infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Possession may be evidence (citations) — see detailed discussion about weight and circumstances in cited sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of attorney — creating patent attorneys, form and revocability
rubrics_metrics.description: Power of attorney forms for creating patent attorneys and limitations on revocability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form of power of attorney, when not revocable (e.g., when part of a contract); see cited sections for form and effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice in equity — procedural rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules of practice in equity relevant to patent litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules of practice in equity collected (citations); see Patent Office regulation references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisites to patent — formal and substantive requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Prerequisites to patent that must be fulfilled or the grant is illegal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be fulfilled; Patent Office and Commissioner authorized to judge; when formal, Commissioner's decision is final; patent is evidence of fulfillment; want of prerequisites and how taken advantage of are discussed (citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle — misuse and patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: Meaning and misuse of the word 'principle' and its relation to patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principle misused in various instances; not an invention and not patentable; cannot be claimed; must be fully described in specification when used; distinctions between principle as force vs idea of means; essential to invention but not itself monopolizable; see long explanatory citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior patent — defined and essential requisites
rubrics_metrics.description: A prior patent used as a defense: its definition and essential requisites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be a public document accessible to the public (secret patent is not); date relative to the invention in question matters; must cover the same invention; be a complete practical invention and fully communicate the invention to the public; later re-issue of older patent is not a prior patent; evidentiary rules cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior publication — as a defense and requisites
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior printed publication as a defense to patent validity and its essential requisites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be printed for general use and put into circulation; written but unpublished descriptions, pictures without text, business circulars/catalogues, patent applications/provisional specs are generally not prior publication; date and sufficiency of description; must describe same invention and fully communicate it to the public; sufficiency may be jury question; rules for proof discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior use — defined and requisites as a defense
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior public use of an invention as a defense to patent validity and its essential requisites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior use defeats patent if it discloses the character of the invention, is complete and practically employed (not merely making), and was public (secret use generally not). Single instance may suffice; evidence requirements; prior use must be identical to invention claimed; prior making, sketches, experiments, etc., may not suffice; provability and burden of proof discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority (between inventors) — conception and diligence
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority determined by priority of conception followed by diligence in reduction to practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Date of conception may be shown; priority is central in interference proceedings; burden of proof is on later patentee; application oath is prima facie evidence; shown by use, publication, or patent; concessions and bindings discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record of patent — constructive notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The recorded patent is notice to all the world (constructive notice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record is notice; actual notice is equivalent; record of unrecordable instrument may not be constructive notice; Patent Office governed by record title; copies and evidentiary uses discussed (citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction to practice — necessity and evidentiary showing
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduction to practice defined and necessary for certain rights; how it is shown and what suffices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defined (actual or constructive); may follow or accompany conception; not shown by application alone unless certain conditions; may be by written description, model, issue of patent; experimental state does not accomplish reduction; must prove invention successful; mechanical perfection not necessary; date of reduction is date of inventive act; best mode and diligence rules; evidentiary showings and citations provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record references and responses — applicant practice
rubrics_metrics.description: What references are cited on rejection of an application and how applicants should answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References, how cited, and how to answer rejections are discussed (citations to Practice before Patent Office sections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public use or sale — defense and effect on abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Public use or sale as a defense to patent and how it may constitute abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public use can be a defence and form of abandonment; abandonment may be presumed from public use; presumption not always rebuttable; experimental use not public use; public use must give knowledge of the invention; use under control/consent of inventor not public use; timing relative to first application matters (e.g., >2 years before application may be abandonment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of inventions by Patent Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent Office's publication of inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noted as a topic (see statutory and procedural rules on Patent Office publications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Purchaser of patented article — right to use
rubrics_metrics.description: Rights of purchasers of patented articles to use them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussed under license/rights entries; purchaser's right to use summarized in cited sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profits — distinction from damages and measure
rubrics_metrics.description: Profits derived from infringement are distinct from damages; rules for computing and measuring profits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Profits are not synonymous with damages; described at law and in equity; may be pecuniary gains actually received from infringement; measure and computation depend on form of infringement; items of cost and yield, sales as measure, burden of proof, theory and limits (remote benefits not included); recoverability rules and accounting procedures discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Property in a patent — twofold nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Property in a patent is twofold (invention and monopoly) and related ownership issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Property distinctions explained; transferability rules and limitations, personal property aspects, effect of assignments and creditors' claims covered in cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process and product — definitions and patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions of process and product when they are inventions and rules on separate patentability and joinder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process distinct from product; both may be separately patentable; may be joined with apparatus/product when appropriate; claims for process, product, and machine have joinder and claim rules; mechanical process claims may be void under some circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior publication vs prior patent vs prior use — evidentiary distinctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Different categories of prior art defenses (publication, patent, use) and their distinct evidentiary requisites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each prior art category has specific requisites: prior patent must be public and cover same invention; prior publication must be printed/circulated and sufficiently descriptive; prior use must be public, complete, and practically employed. Proof, dates, and exceptions are discussed in each section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue — scope, conditions, and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-issue as a statutory mode to amend letters-patent; conditions when permitted and limits on new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Origin and statutory background; re-issue available only under statutory conditions for imperfect patents; not allowed to add new matter beyond what original described and attempted to claim; cannot expand invention or include improvements/new matter; identity with original presumed until contrary shown; re-issue cannot cure a void ab initio patent; re-issue may amend defective description or excessive claim but limited to subject-matter attempted to be described and claimed in original; identity determined by comparing specifications, drawings, and models; courts/Patent Office follow same rules; many specific limits and presumptions detailed (citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehearing in equity — new defenses or evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for rehearing in equity to let in new defenses or new evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires supplemental bill for new evidence; Patent Office rules and grounds for rehearing cited; how courts handle new evidence and defenses explained in cited sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record and evidence — private writings & recollections
rubrics_metrics.description: Role of private writings and witness recollections as evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private writings discussed as evidence; weight of recollections of witnesses considered; evidentiary treatment and limitations cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receivers and patents — vesting and conveyance
rubrics_metrics.description: Effect of receivership on patent title and ability to convey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents do not vest in receivers to convey legal title; may convey equitable title; limitations under state laws; receivers acting under court orders protected from interference; cross-references for special circumstances.
